sessions.title: A Tutorial for Kokkos: Performance Portability for C++ Applications and Libraries
sessions.speakers: Yuuichi Asahi, Luc Berger-Vergiat, Patrick Diehl, Hariprasad Kannan
sessions.description: This SC26 tutorial on Kokkos — an HPC, performance portability, open source, C++ library — targets a beginner audience who wants to write efficient code for CPU and GPU hardware, while maintaining only one code base. The course consists of lectures and hands-on exercises, covering the fundamental aspects of the Kokkos library, including parallel construct functions and memory management classes. The materials come from the official, open source Kokkos tutorial, which is freely accessible online. This is a full-day tutorial.

sessions.title: Accelerated Quantum Supercomputing: A Hands-On Tutorial on Quantum-Classical Hybrid Workflows Executed on QPUs and GPUs
sessions.speakers: Michael Williams de la Bastida, Minh Chung, Danny Bulmash, Zohim Chandani
sessions.description: Accelerated quantum supercomputing (AQSC) requires engineers to consider the hardware, software, and infrastructure challenges that arise when integrating quantum processing units (QPUs) into an HPC environment. This tutorial will provide attendees with hands-on experience to learn about AQSC infrastructure being deployed at supercomputing centers around the world. Participants will gain hands-on experience with the Python API of CUDA-Q. Attendees will have access to GPUs and IQM QPUs hosted at Leibniz Supercomputing Centre (LRZ). Live demonstrations and hands-on exercises include how to scale workflows, from a simple pip install to deploying multi-GPU, multi-node, and QPU jobs. This will all be tied under two quantum algorithms: sample-based Krylov quantum diagonalization (SKQD: quantum and HPC) and generative quantum eigensolver (GQE: AI and quantum), emphasizing the need for HPC and…

sessions.title: Compression for AI and Scientific Data
sessions.speakers: Franck Cappello, Peter Lindstrom, Robert R. Underwood
sessions.description: Large-scale numerical simulations, experimental instruments, observational platforms, and modern AI workloads generate and consume unprecedented volumes of data, creating critical challenges for storage, I/O, communication, and analysis. Data compression—particularly error-bounded lossy compression—is a key enabling technology to address these challenges. This half-day tutorial reviews the motivations, fundamental principles, and algorithmic foundations of lossy compression for scientific and AI data workflows. It introduces core compression stages (decorrelation, approximation, and encoding) and examines their realizations in state-of-the-art compressors. It emphasizes trustworthiness through error control, uncertainty quantification, and application-specific quality metrics. New this year, we consistently incorporate compression for AI and data-driven workflows, including training…

sessions.title: Core-Level Performance Engineering
sessions.speakers: Jan Laukemann, Georg Hager, Filippo Spiga
sessions.description: While many developers put a lot of effort into optimizing large-scale parallelism, they often neglect the importance of an efficient serial code. Even worse, slow serial code tends to scale very well, hiding the fact that resources are wasted because no definite hardware performance limit (“bottleneck”) is exhausted. This tutorial conveys the required knowledge to develop a thorough understanding of the interactions between software and hardware on the level of a single CPU core and the lowest memory hierarchy level (the L1 cache). We introduce general out-of-order core architectures and their typical performance bottlenecks using modern x86-64 (Intel Sapphire Rapids) and ARM (NVIDIA Vera) processors as examples. We then go into detail about x86 and AArch64 assembly code, specifically including vectorization (SIMD), pipeline utilization, critical paths, and loop-carried dependencies.…

sessions.title: Deep Learning at Scale: Engineering High-Resolution Scientific AI Models
sessions.speakers: Shashank Subramanian, Steven Farrell, Josh Romero, Thorsten Kurth, Corneel Casert, Adam Rupe
sessions.description: Deep learning is increasingly used in scientific applications involving high-dimensional, high-resolution data. As models, datasets, and data resolutions scale, so does the need for efficient, distributed training on high performance computing (HPC) systems. This tutorial addresses practical challenges in training scientific AI models on high-resolution data, including data throughput, memory pressure, and communication overhead in distributed HPC workflows. Participants will learn to profile and build efficient data pipelines, optimize single-GPU performance, and scale training across GPUs and nodes using data, tensor, and spatial (domain) parallelism. Through hands-on examples drawn from scientific use cases, we will show how different model families, such as transformers, convolutional neural networks, and neural operators, benefit from these parallelization strategies. We will…

sessions.title: Efficient Distributed GPU Programming for Exascale
sessions.speakers: Andreas Herten, Simon Garcia de Gonzalo, Jiri Kraus, Lena Oden, Oded Green
sessions.description: Over the past decade, GPUs became ubiquitous in HPC installations around the world, delivering the majority of performance of some of the largest supercomputers, steadily increasing the available compute capacity. Four exascale systems (Frontier, Aurora, El Capitan, JUPITER) use GPUs as the core computing devices. To take advantage of these GPU-accelerated systems with tens of thousands of devices, application developers need to have the proper skills and tools to understand, manage, and optimize distributed GPU applications. In this tutorial, participants will learn techniques to efficiently program large-scale multi-GPU systems. While programming multiple GPUs with MPI is explained, also advanced tuning techniques and complementing programming models like NCCL and NVSHMEM are presented. Tools for analysis are shown and used to motivate and implement performance optimizations. The…

sessions.title: Flux: Workload Management for HPC and AI/ML Simulation in Cloud
sessions.speakers: Vanessa Sochat, Daniel Milroy, Tom Scogland, William Hobbs
sessions.description: Modern scientific workloads require automation and elasticity beyond the reach of traditional HPC schedulers. Developed over a decade at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, Flux is the next-generation workload manager powering El Capitan, the world's #1 exascale system. Flux is unique for its graph-based, hierarchical resource management, enabling seamless portability and performance for complex workflows. Recently, the project joined the High Performance Software Foundation (HPSF) and was integrated with the Kubernetes Kubeflow Trainer for AI/ML. Participants will explore Flux foundations before diving into advanced capabilities for on-premises, cloud, and Kubernetes environments. We will cover the orchestration of heterogeneous workloads that require interplay between simulation, analysis, and services. Through lectures and hands-on, energetic tutorials that include interactive…

sessions.title: High-Performance and Smart-Networking Technologies for HPC and AI
sessions.speakers: Dhabaleswar K. Panda, Benjamin Michalowicz, Tu Tran, Goutham Kalikrishna Reddy Kuncham, Noah Klein, Sungjae Lee
sessions.description: High-performance networking technologies are generating a lot of excitement towards building next-generation high-end computing (HEC) systems for HPC and AI with hundreds of thousands of servers with the latest CPU and GPU technologies, and a variety of application workloads. This tutorial provides an overview of these emerging technologies, their architectural features, current market standing, and suitability for designing HEC systems while delivering scale-up and scale-out principles. We present a holistic view of the major scale-out interconnects that power today’s supercomputers, such as IB, HSE, RoCE, Omni-Path, AWS-EFA, Slingshot, Tofu-D, and Ultra-Ethernet Consortium, followed by scale-up interconnects like NVLink/NVSwitch, AMD Infinity Fabric, CXL, and ESUN. We also highlight how the features of these networking technologies are integrated into libraries such as UCX,…

sessions.title: In-Network Computing with SmartNICs for HPC Applications
sessions.speakers: Elie Kfoury, Jeffrey Young, Richard Graham, Antonio Peña, Paul Ruth, Jorge Crichigno +1
sessions.description: The past few years have witnessed an increased level of support for and deployment of programmable network adapters, known as "SmartNICs." These enhanced network devices offer standard packet processing capabilities as well as advanced "in-network" computing features built around programmable lightweight processing cores, FPGAs, and even CPU- and GPU-based platforms capable of running separate operating systems. SmartNICs have gained rapid adoption for data center tasks, including infrastructure management, packet filtering, and I/O acceleration. Increasingly these devices are also being explored for high-performance computing (HPC) and AI application acceleration. This tutorial provides an in-depth exploration of the state of the art in SmartNICs and the emerging software ecosystems that support them. Attendees will participate in hands-on exercises designed to demonstrate how…

sessions.title: Introduction to MLIR
sessions.speakers: Ponnuswamy Sadayappan, Mahesh Ravishankar, Kunwar Grover, Atanas Rountev
sessions.description: MLIR is rapidly becoming the infrastructure of choice for building domain-specific languages (DSLs) and compilers for high performance computing — examples include OpenAI’s Triton, NVIDIA’s cuTile, and AMD’s AIR/AIE. Dialects are a core concept in MLIR, enabling data types and operations to be defined at different levels of abstraction, along with passes to systematically transform the programs through a hierarchy of dialects for optimized execution on target platforms. In-tree dialects like Linalg define operations that can represent common computation paradigms like tensor contractions and convolutions. This tutorial will introduce MLIR and provide an understanding of the steps to build a DSL compiler to target CPUs and GPUs. Starting with an overview of core MLIR concepts, like dialects, operations, types and interfaces, the tutorial will give participants hands-on experience in…

sessions.title: Parallel Computing 101
sessions.speakers: Quentin Stout, Christiane Jablonowski
sessions.description: This tutorial provides a comprehensive overview of parallel computing, emphasizing those aspects most relevant to the user. It is suitable for new users, students, managers, and anyone seeking an overview of parallel computing. It discusses software and hardware/software interaction, with an emphasis on standards, portability, and systems that are widely available. The tutorial surveys basic parallel computing concepts, using examples from multiple engineering, scientific, machine learning, and data analysis problems. These examples illustrate using MPI on distributed memory systems; OpenMP on shared memory systems; MPI+OpenMP on hybrid systems; and CUDA or compiler directives on GPUs and accelerators. It discusses numerous parallelization and load balancing approaches; performance improvement tools; and an overview of recent developments such as machine learning on accelerators and…

sessions.title: Programming Your GPU with OpenMP: A “Hands-On” Introduction
sessions.speakers: Tim Mattson, Bob Robey, Michael Klemm, Johanna Potyka
sessions.description: If you are an HPC programmer, you know the OpenMP® API. Alongside MPI, the OpenMP API is the open, cross-vendor foundation of HPC. As hardware complexity has grown, the OpenMP programming model has grown as well, adding GPU support in OpenMP 4.0 (2013). With over a decade of evolution since then, OpenMP GPU technology is a mature option for programming any GPU you are likely to find on the market. While there are many ways to program a GPU, the best way is through the OpenMP API. Why? Because the GPU does not exist in isolation. There are always one or more CPUs on a node. Programmers need portable code that fully exploits all available processors. In other words, programmers need a programming model, such as OpenMP, that fully embraces heterogeneity. In this tutorial, we explore GPU programming with the OpenMP programming model. We assume attendees are familiar with multithreading, so…

On GPU-accelerated platforms, developers face a key diagnostic gap: profilers show where stalls occur but provide limited dependency paths explaining why. Her work included evaluating the patentability and commercialization potential of university innovations, negotiating legal…

sessions.title: Advanced Architecture Testbeds: Community Resources for HPC-AI Research
sessions.speakers: Jeffrey Young, Jens Domke, Murali Emani, Steve Moulton, Oscar Hernandez, Filippo Spiga
sessions.description: Testbeds play a vital role in assessing the readiness of novel architectures for upcoming supercomputers for the exascale and post-exascale era. These testbeds also act as co-design hubs, enabling the collection of application operational requirements, while identifying critical gaps that need to be addressed for an architecture to become viable for HPC. Various research centers are actively deploying testbeds, and our aim is to build a community that facilitates the sharing of information, encouraging collaboration and understanding of the available evaluation resources. This BoF will facilitate the exchange of best practices, including testbed design, benchmarking, system evaluation, and availability.

sessions.title: Beyond the GPU: The Future of AI Acceleration in the Zettascale Era
sessions.speakers: Torsten Hoefler, Satoshi Matsuoka, Rob Schreiber, Jeff Hammond, Tal Ben-Nun, Steve Scott
sessions.description: The rapid evolution of AI is driving unprecedented innovation in computing architectures, from GPUs and AI accelerators to novel memory, networking, and system designs. This BoF brings together leaders from industry, academia, and national laboratories to discuss emerging directions in AI acceleration for future zettascale systems. Rather than focusing on specific products, participants will explore common challenges in architecture, programmability, scalability, energy efficiency, software ecosystems, and deployment at scale. The session will emphasize audience interaction, community discussion, and roadmap development, providing attendees an opportunity to help shape the future of AI acceleration and AI-enabled supercomputing.

sessions.title: Data Readiness for AI in HPC: Building a Community Around Dimensions, Metrics, and Tools
sessions.speakers: Suren Byna, Jean Luca Bez, Wes Brewer, Shreyas Cholia
sessions.description: AI now drives discovery across HPC science, yet models are only as trustworthy as the data they use. Many teams still lack a shared way to judge whether their data is ready for AI. This BoF brings together the HPC and scientific communities to define data readiness for AI using seven practical dimensions: quality, understandability, fair and unbiased representation, structure and organization, feature importance, governance covering ethics, security and privacy, and AI-specific needs such as labels and distributions. Through short talks and open discussion, we will compare practices, identify gaps, and begin building shared metrics, tools, and benchmarks.

sessions.title: Ethics in HPC: With Great Power Comes Great Responsibility
sessions.speakers: Jay Lofstead, Jakob Luettgau, Elaine Raybourn
sessions.description: The implications of HPC technology on society and the environment prompt us, as a community, to discuss and understand our direct and indirect impacts. This BoF is highly interactive and aims to facilitate discussion within the community, relating ethical behavior and societal norms to the design of HPC solutions and autonomous/intelligent systems. The BoF will feature breakout groups and then converge to a plenum discussion. By furthering this dialogue, we can ensure that the HPC community advances its commitment to technology for the benefit of humanity as a whole. We do not expect to reach conclusions, but raise ideas.

sessions.title: HPC Procurement, Energy Efficiency, and Sustainability
sessions.track: Architectures, Networks, State of the Practice
sessions.speakers: Ayesha Afzal, Natalie Bates, Yutong Lu, Masaaki Kondo, Maria Grazia Giuffreda, Jim Rogers
sessions.description: Energy efficiency has evolved from an operational objective into a contractual engineering requirement for next-generation HPC systems. This BoF explores how procurement contracts shape future supercomputer design by comparing approaches from China, Japan, and Europe. Yutong Lu examines the architectural evolution from Tianhe-2A to CPU-based LineShine, highlighting CPU-based acceleration methods without relying on accelerator components. Masaaki Kondo presents Fugaku to FugakuNEXT, emphasizing procurement strategies for higher simulation performance within a power envelope. Maria Grazia Giuffreda discusses energy-to-solution requirements and software optimization clauses. An interactive forum debates how procurement clauses drive architectural choices, software portability, sustainability, and innovation in late-2020s deployments.

sessions.title: Julia for HPC
sessions.speakers: William Godoy, Evelyne Ringoot, Vicki Carrica, Mose Giordano, Rabab Alomairy, Felipe Tomé +6
sessions.description: The “Julia for HPC” BoF provides a place for the HPC community with interests in the Julia programming language as an LLVM front-end to close the gaps between high-productivity languages and the performance of compiled languages. We invite participants from industry, government, and academia to discuss their experiences, identify and learn about opportunities and gaps. Topics include Julia adoption for quantum computing, auto-tuning, mixed precision, and agentic AI. The fifth consecutive BoF continues the “Julia for HPC” engagement with the SC community, and complements the tutorial on Julia for HPC at SC26. Presentations will be posted here: https://github.com/JuliaParallel/julia-hpc-bof-sc26.

sessions.title: Mixed Feelings About Mixed Precisions
sessions.speakers: Hatem Ltaief, Piotr Luszczek, Hartwig Anzt, Harun Bayraktar, Nicholas Malaya
sessions.description: What if we have been oversolving in computational science and engineering for decades? Are low-precision arithmetic formats only for AI workloads? How can HPC applications exploit mixed-precision hardware features? This BoF invites the HPC community at large interested in applying mixed precisions into their workflows and discussing the impact on time-to-solution, memory footprint, storage, data motion, and energy consumption. Experts from scientific applications/software libraries/hardware architectures will briefly provide the context on this trendy topic, share their own perspectives, and mostly engage with the audience via a set of questions, while gathering feedback to define a roadmap moving forward.

sessions.title: Open-Source Hardware Tools: Advancing Architecture Research and Chip Prototyping
sessions.speakers: Kazutomo Yoshii, Kentaro Sano, John Shalf, Antonino Tumeo, Junichiro Kadomoto, Franz Franchetti
sessions.description: As demand for specialized architectures grows in the post-Moore era, this BoF will foster a sustained community around chip prototyping using open-source hardware tools. Building on themes explored in previous editions of this BoF at SC24 and SC25, the session will focus on practical tool experiences, current gaps, domain-specific accelerators, AI-assisted design workflows, and chip prototyping as an emerging HPC workload. Invited speakers from architecture, open-source EDA, accelerator design, and HPC will seed discussion. Expected outcomes include actionable insights, stronger collaboration, and follow-up community initiatives to advance open-source chip prototyping.

sessions.title: OpenCHAMI Community Birds of a Feather
sessions.speakers: Alex Lovell-Troy, Jay Depasse, John Lockman, Sadaf Alam
sessions.description: HPC centers are modernizing how they provision and operate clusters as systems become more heterogeneous, security-sensitive, and composable. OpenCHAMI, an HPSF emerging project, is an operator-led open-source control plane that brings cloud-like APIs and modular services to HPC system management. This BoF will help newcomers understand what OpenCHAMI enables today, give current users a forum to compare deployments and priorities, and invite operators, vendors, and developers to shape the roadmap. We will discuss adoption paths, including but not limited to xCAT transitions, and collect community feedback on tooling, integration, documentation, and operational requirements.

sessions.title: OpenSHMEM: Toward a Unified GPU-Aware Auxiliary Specification and 2.0
sessions.speakers: Stephen Poole, Oscar Hernandez, Michael Beebe, Naveen Namashivayam, Benjamin Michalowicz, Manjunath Gorentla Venkata +4
sessions.description: OpenSHMEM is a community-driven partitioned global address space (PGAS) API for low-overhead, one-sided asynchronous communication across diverse HPC architectures. This BoF will present progress since the 1.6 specification and discuss ongoing work toward OpenSHMEM 1.7, the proposed GPU auxiliary specification for accelerator support, and the longer-term OpenSHMEM 2.0 roadmap. As heterogeneous systems become the norm, the session will bring together users, implementers, middleware and tool developers, hardware vendors, and HPC facilities to share experiences, discuss evolving requirements, and help shape a simple, portable, and vendor-neutral future for OpenSHMEM.

sessions.title: Reproducibility of Computational Research: Building a Community of Practice for the AI Era
sessions.speakers: Hakizumwami Runesha, Benjamin Lynch, Sandra Gesing
sessions.description: Reproducibility remains a fundamental challenge for computational science and AI-enabled research. Building on successful BoFs at SC22, SC24, and PEARC22-PEARC25, we established the Reproducibility of Computational Research Community of Practice, which now includes an active mailing list, public website, webinar series, and emerging working groups. This interactive BoF will engage the SC26 community in shaping the next phase of this effort by sharing community progress, launching working groups, and exploring how AI can improve the capture of reproducible computational artifacts while addressing new challenges. The session welcomes researchers, research computing professionals, software developers, librarians, and cyberinfrastructure practitioners.

sessions.title: SIGHPC Annual Member Meeting
sessions.speakers: Christine Harvey, Michela Taufer
sessions.description: The SIGHPC Annual Member Meeting brings together ACM SIGHPC members and the broader HPC community to review the organization's activities, celebrate recent accomplishments, and discuss priorities for the coming year. The meeting provides an open forum where members can interact directly with SIGHPC leadership, learn about ongoing initiatives in education, awards, student programs, chapters, diversity and inclusion, publications, and conference activities, and help shape future directions. Whether you are a long-time member or new to the community, this session offers an opportunity to engage with SIGHPC leadership, provide feedback, ask questions, and become involved in the society's activities.

sessions.title: The Future of Python on HPC Systems
sessions.speakers: Andy Terrel, Todd Gamblin, Davin Potts, Quynh Nguyen
sessions.description: Python is the most widely used programming language today — but on HPC systems, it’s often more pain than power. From slow module loading on shared filesystems to packaging headaches and incompatible distributions, these hurdles block new users and frustrate seasoned developers alike. Meanwhile, major changes to Python’s core — new array APIs, packaging reforms, JIT compilation, and threading primitives — are happening without HPC at the table. This BoF brings together language leaders and HPC practitioners to shape Python’s future, learn what’s coming, and connect with peers.

sessions.title: The Impact of GenAI on HPC Programming and Programming Models
sessions.speakers: Bradford Chamberlain, Rosa Badia, Martin Schulz, Christian Terboven, Michael Garland, Chris Siefert
sessions.description: According to many mainstream media outlets and tech gurus, the age of computer programmers is fading away as GenAI proves itself capable of helping with programming tasks, or completing them independently. And many of us probably have positive (and negative) stories about using AI in our day-to-day lives. But what do we expect the impact of GenAI to be on programming for HPC systems and applications? This session kicks off with opening statements from thought leaders representing various HPC programming models (MPI, OpenMP, NVIDIA, Kokkos, COMPSs, and Chapel), followed by an open session for audience opinions, Q&A, and healthy debate.

sessions.title: The Status and Future of Unified Shared Memory in the CPU+GPU Ecosystem
sessions.speakers: Igor Sfiligoi, Amit Ruhela, Austin Ellis, Flavio Galeazzo, Reuben Budiarja, Todd Evans
sessions.description: Originally GPU and CPU memory spaces were completely separate, with explicit data movements needed for interaction between CPU and GPU compute cores. Over time, all major GPU vendors have added hardware and software capabilities for transparent access to each other’s memory, with various levels of granularity and integration, with unified shared memory (USM) representing the most tight integration. This BoF will start by outlining the history, current state, and planned future of cross-memory technologies. We will then open the floor for discussion with conference attendees to gather their perspectives on where this technology should evolve going forward.

sessions.title: Workflows Community: Next-Generation Workflows for HPC — AI, Agentic Systems, and Scientific Discovery
sessions.speakers: Stephen Hudson, Kyle Chard, Rafael Ferreira da Silva, Daniela Cassol, Woong Shin, Mathew Cherukara +2
sessions.description: This BoF will convene the workflows community to discuss the challenges of next-generation scientific workflows. A central focus will be on how the role of the human changes as workflows become increasingly autonomous: where people remain in the loop, how they steer and validate agentic systems, and how our community can support workflow developers. The session will bring together workflow users, developers, theorists, and industrial collaborators, highlighting emerging research directions and practical needs from scientific campaigns. Through interactive discussions, participants will explore collaborative strategies to enable resilient, scalable, and adaptive workflows that meet the evolving demands of scientific discovery.

Drawing on experience from the NSF ICICLE AI Institute and invited external perspectives, participants will debate autonomy levels, trust, provenance, evaluation, and emerging protocols such as MCP, and identify steps toward community benchmarks and interoperable agentic cyberinfrastructure.

sessions.speakers: Fernando Posada, Carla Osthoff, Esteban Hernandez, Silvio Rizzi, Carlos Barrios Hernandez, Philippe Navaux +1
sessions.description: Building on a decade of Americas HPC Collaboration (AHPC) BoFs, this SC26 session will formalize the Education and Workforce Development Chapter and outline a practical roadmap for its first year. The BoF will focus on areas where collaboration can make a concrete impact: system-facing training for people who deploy and support HPC/AI infrastructure, using the Oak Ridge Computing Academy (ORCA) as one example; a panel on emerging AI and quantum training needs with academia and industry participants; and student cluster competition experiences that demonstrate the value of hands-on learning. Participants will identify shared assets, pilot activities, and institutional commitments.

sessions.title: Blended Infrastructure for Advanced Computational Workflows: From Accelerated Discovery to Agentic Automation
sessions.speakers: Felix Schürmann, Jay Boisseau, Ilkay Altintas De Callafon, Costas Bekas, Fernanda Foertter, Bob Sorensen +1
sessions.description: As HPC accelerates into an era of hybrid infrastructure and pervasive AI, computational research increasingly calls for optimizing blended on-prem and cloud infrastructure for advanced workflows that will accelerate future discoveries. This session begins with the drivers: cutting-edge science workflows challenging traditional infrastructure, and agentic AI workflows that autonomously drive the entire scientific loop from hypothesis generation to results analysis. We then review the current capabilities and gaps for managing and using blended HPC infrastructure as the backbone of these advanced workflows. Attendees will engage in discussion and interactive polling, collaboratively identifying gaps and opportunities for the community to address.

sessions.title: Building the Scientific Data Fabric Community for AI-Driven Discovery
sessions.speakers: Michela Taufer, Valerio Pascucci, Carol Song, Virginia Trueheart, David Kanter
sessions.description: Artificial intelligence is transforming scientific discovery, but today's cyberinfrastructure was designed for workflows in which data are collected, stored, analyzed, and archived as largely independent activities. Modern science increasingly requires continuous interaction among instruments, data repositories, workflows, AI services, edge devices, HPC systems, and scientists across institutional boundaries. This BoF brings together researchers, facility operators, cyberinfrastructure developers, and domain scientists to discuss the next generation of scientific data infrastructure. Through examples from astronomy, geosciences, materials science, medicine, and high-energy physics, participants will identify common infrastructure challenges and define a community roadmap for interoperable, federated scientific data ecosystems.

sessions.title: Confidential Supercomputing: Essential Evolution or Elegant Illusion?
sessions.speakers: Sadaf Alam, Hai Ah Nam, Albert Reuther, Nathaniel McCallum, Nigel Edwards, CJ Newburn +1
sessions.description: Sensitive workloads across health sciences, financial modeling, and AI/ML on proprietary data increasingly demand confidentiality guarantees traditionally out of scope for supercomputing infrastructure. Confidential computing—hardware-enforced trusted execution environments established in cloud and edge contexts—is proposed as a path to securing computation at HPC scale. But is this achievable, or does it conflict with the principles that make supercomputers fast? This BoF gathers the HPC community to debate whether confidential supercomputing is a necessary, achievable evolution or an aspirational posture satisfying compliance optics without meaningful security. Join us to map where it genuinely delivers—and where gaps remain.

sessions.title: Digital Twins in HPC: From Shared Definitions to Shared Standards
sessions.speakers: Barton Fiske, Andrea Townsend-Nicholson, Dan Isaacs
sessions.description: The HPC community now has a working definition of the digital twin, anchored in the 2024 NASEM report. What it lacks are standards to operationalize that definition across the full lifecycle. This BoF brings together practitioners from novice to expert, spanning scientific computing, biomedicine, infrastructure, and data centers, to surface the most urgent gaps: data homogenization across heterogeneous sources, verification, validation, and uncertainty quantification (VVUQ) at every lifecycle stage, and the emerging role of agentic AI as both enabler and new source of complexity. We will map the landscape, identify active efforts, and determine what coordinated community action looks like.

sessions.title: Ecosystems for Scientific Computing in the Age of AI
sessions.speakers: Lois Curfman McInnes, Anshu Dubey, Dorian Arnold, Prasanna Balaprakash, Mike Bernhardt, Thomas Herault +4
sessions.description: AI is rapidly reshaping scientific software through code generation, simulation acceleration, intelligent workflows, and emerging agentic systems. Yet the software ecosystems, collaboration models, trust frameworks, and workforce practices that underpin high performance computing (HPC) were built for a different era. Drawing on findings from a recent workshop series (https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.03413), this BoF invites the international community to challenge assumptions, identify emerging priorities, and help define the next generation of scientific computing ecosystems. Discussion will focus on human-AI collaboration, trust, sustainability, user experience, and workforce evolution — turning shared insights into actionable directions for the community.

sessions.title: HPC Carpentry: A New Carpentries Lesson Program
sessions.speakers: Andrew Reid, Wirawan Purwanto, Trevor Keller, Alan O'Cais, Annajiat Alim Rasel, Benson Muite
sessions.description: The HPC Carpentry project, an effort to provide hands-on workshop-based instruction for novice users of HPC systems, has long been well-aligned with the broader educational mission of the Carpentries project, using open-source materials to bridge the gap between resources and the skills needed to use them effectively. Having been adopted as a new lesson program within the Carpentries, it is time to reconnect with the larger HPC community, seeking feedback on strategic planning, and identifying new audiences where the solutions developed during the Carpentries incubation and adoption process can add value and strengthen the world of HPC education.

sessions.title: HPC Graph Toolkits and the GraphBLAS Forum
sessions.speakers: Antonino Tumeo, Timothy Mattson, Jose Moreira
sessions.description: Graph analytics is foundational to scientific discovery, national security, artificial intelligence (AI), and industrial innovation, yet sparse, irregular, and evolving graph workloads continue to challenge HPC systems. This BoF convenes developers and users of high-performance graph toolkits to exchange updates, compare combinatorial and algebraic approaches, and define priorities for converged workflows spanning simulation, data analytics, AI, instruments, edge platforms, clouds, and supercomputers. Discussion will address GraphBLAS, interoperability, dynamic graphs, heterogeneous execution, provenance, trustworthy reasoning, and sustainable open infrastructure, producing concrete community directions for research, software, standards, benchmarks, infrastructure investment, and cross-sector collaboration. The outcome will guide collaborative work beyond SC26.

sessions.title: Liquid Cooling Interfaces: Optimizing Temperature, Telemetry, Water, and Heat Reuse
sessions.track: Power and Energy, State of the Practice, Sustainability
sessions.speakers: Jeff Autor, David Martinez, Tiziano Belotti, Steven Martin, Karsten Kutzer, Chris DePrater +2
sessions.description: As direct liquid cooling scales, the interface between IT systems and facility mechanical infrastructure becomes more critical. This BoF explores four challenges. First, high-temperature cooling (heat-reuse, IT thermal margins) and dew point (prevent condensation). Second, warm-water fluid quality (filtration and added chemicals to prevent corrosion, biological growth, and scaling). Third, temperature and fluid dynamics with rapid workload power swings (volumetric expansion, pump cavitation, facility response characteristics). Fourth, integrating telemetry into IT systems and building automation (predict thermal excursions, reduce trapped capacity). This session is intended for facility engineers, system integrators, operations, administrators, architects, and researchers in energy-efficiency and sustainability.

sessions.title: OpenACC Forum — The Future of Programming Accelerators with Directives
sessions.speakers: Daniel Howard, Fernanda Foertter, Jack Wells, Thomas Schwinge
sessions.description: Through its mission to reduce time to science by nurturing parallel computing skills, the Open Accelerated Computing Consortium (OpenACC) invites you to explore the future of directive-based programming. In the age of agentic coding assistants, this BoF examines the evolving roles of OpenACC, OpenMP, standard language parallelism, and abstraction libraries like Julia for Accelerators or Kokkos for GPU-resident runtimes. Panels including compiler developers and community leaders will summarize the current state of programming for accelerators, followed by open discussion comparing practices and imagining new futures. Developers, researchers, compiler vendors, and the broader HPC community are welcome to shape the conversation.

TOP500 Supercomputers
sessions.speakers: Erich Strohmaier, Jack Dongarra, Horst Simon, Christine Harvey
sessions.description: The TOP500 list of supercomputers serves as a “Who’s Who” in the field of high performance computing (HPC). It started as a list of the most powerful supercomputers in the world and has evolved to a major source of information about trends in HPC. The 68th TOP500 list will be published in November 2026, just in time for SC26. This BoF will present detailed analyses of the TOP500 and discuss the changes in the HPC marketplace during the past years. The BoF is meant as an open forum for discussion and feedback between the TOP500 authors and the user community.

sessions.title: Training Without Sharing: Federated Learning on the World's HPC Systems for Science
sessions.speakers: Sagar Dolas, Olivera Kotevska, Tim Kok, Chester Chen
sessions.description: Federated learning (FL) lets institutions train shared AI models without exchanging raw data — a capability increasingly essential for science where data is sensitive, proprietary, or too large to move. Yet FL on HPC remains uncharted: job schedulers, site firewalls, identity federation, and heterogeneous accelerators reshape the problem beyond what cloud-based FL assumes. This BoF brings together framework developers, HPC centers, and scientific users to discuss running trustworthy FL across the world's supercomputers. We will surface open algorithmic, systems, and governance challenges and work toward a community roadmap for cross-facility FL benchmarks, interoperability, and shared practice.

sessions.title: U.S. National Science Foundation Cyberinfrastructure in an Age of Change and Challenge
sessions.speakers: Daniel Reed, Todd Gamblin, Willam Gropp, Torsten Hoefler, Ruth Marinshaw, Michael Norman +4
sessions.description: The U.S. National Science Foundation asked the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine to assess the evolving role of cyberinfrastructure in enabling 21st-century scientific discovery and innovation. This Birds of a Feather session will discuss the committee’s assessment of NSF’s advanced cyberinfrastructure portfolio in a rapidly changing environment shaped by artificial intelligence, cloud computing, rapidly expanding private-sector investment in AI, and the potential role of strategic partnership between government and industry. Committee members will summarize major themes from the report and invite community discussion on how NSF can sustain broad, effective, and forward-looking cyberinfrastructure for the research enterprise.

sessions.title: Who and What Is on Your Machine? Meeting the Coming Rules for Shared AI Compute Without Slowing the Science
sessions.speakers: Saber Feki, Yang Guo, Stephen Green, Kevin DeVilbiss
sessions.description: HPC systems were built for trusted users. Today they run a variety of HPC and AI workloads, serve GPU-as-a-service customers they've never met, and face rising regulatory attention. NIST is finalizing SP 800-234, the first HPC-specific security overlay, and advanced compute is one of the few genuinely bipartisan topics in Washington. The rules are coming. The question is whether operators shape them or inherit them. This BoF brings standards authors, security architects, supercomputing operators, and implementers into a candid, practitioner-level exchange with the audience on what works, what fails, and how the community secures shared compute without slowing the science.

Science gateways, workflow systems, and remote development tools initiate SSH-mediated actions…

Existing lossy compressors such as SZ3 operate in data space and provide no guarantees on downstream visualization fidelity. sessions.title: A Single Pane of Glass for AI Supercomputing: Interoperable Access Portals Worldwide
sessions.speakers: Sadaf Alam, Ilja Livenson, Evangelos FLOROS, Thomas Berger, Ashley Atkins, Tom Green
sessions.description: Providing simplified access to distributed HPC, AI, and cloud resources is a global challenge. Driven by major investments and user demand for a single pane of glass, the need for interoperable resource portals is clear—yet implementations that work across institutional and national boundaries remain hard. Following a well-received ISC 2026 BoF, this session broadens the conversation to operators of federated research infrastructures across Europe, the U.S., and Asia-Pacific, sharing experiences, challenges overcome, and lessons learned. Through lightning updates, live polling, and moderated discussion, attendees exchange practical approaches to federated identity, allocation, accounting, and site autonomy versus federated consistency.

sessions.title: Applications, Libraries, and Tools in Modern Fortran (alt.fortran)
sessions.speakers: Katherine Rasmussen, Christopher Maynard, Thomas Clune, Liam Pattinson, Wael Elwasif, Manuel Arenaz +1
sessions.description: Fortran plays a crucial role in numerous applications. This BoF provides a forum for Fortran developers to engage with the language's modern programming features. With features introduced in recent language revisions, Fortran 2023 supports modern programming practices and high performance computing (HPC). This BoF gathers developers from diverse domains to share experiences and explore Fortran's evolving capabilities. After some brief presentations, the session will focus on an interactive discussion where audience members will be encouraged to share their own experiences and ask questions of our experts.

sessions.title: Autonomous Science Network: A Grassroots Community for Trustworthy Science
sessions.speakers: Rafael Ferreira da Silva, Michela Taufer, Tom Gibbs, Ravinder Kapoor, Arvind Ramanathan
sessions.description: Autonomous experiment operation is demonstrating the ability to dramatically improve the pace of scientific discovery. This BoF convenes a community to continue building on the early two-year roadmap, discussing how different teams are using agentic workflows to improve the potential for new discovery and to address the related need to verify the new results.

sessions.title: Communication Libraries in HPC and AI
sessions.speakers: Nikoli Dryden, Shelby Lockhart, Didem Unat, Jeff Hammond
sessions.description: The world's largest supercomputers for scientific discovery are also premier systems for artificial intelligence model training and inference. While traditional HPC compute has predominately leveraged the MPI standard, AI workloads have increasingly focused on collective communication libraries, such as NVIDIA's NCCL and AMD's RCCL, which are optimized for high throughput and GPU-native usage. This Birds of a Feather (BoF) session at the SC Conference (SC) aims to delve into the intricacies of collective communication libraries, focusing on the comparison between the widely adopted Message Passing Interface (MPI) and NCCL/RCCL, as well as other key messaging libraries, such as SHMEM.

sessions.title: Correctness Testing of HPC Scientific Software in the Age of AI-Generated Code
sessions.speakers: Keita Teranishi, Manish Motwani, Jeffrey Young, Swaroop Pophale, Ignacio Laguna
sessions.description: Effective software testing plays a critical role in guaranteeing the performance, correctness, and reproducibility of software. Testing high-performance computing (HPC) software poses unique challenges due to massive parallelism, concurrency and heterogeneity, the scale of target platforms, lack of oracles, and application-specific verification and verification. These challenges are now amplified by AI coding tools generating and translating HPC code faster than humans can review it. In this BoF, a panel of experts and the audience will discuss methodologies and challenges in HPC software testing, including verification of AI-generated code to deepen our understanding of this crucial aspect of HPC software development.

sessions.title: HPC Developments for Fusion Energy Applications
sessions.speakers: Quynh Nguyen, Shantenu Jha, Justin Angus, Nitin Shukla
sessions.description: The growing interest in fusion energy to power massive data centers has created an urgent need to accelerate plasma science codes. Both experimental capabilities and computational workflows are complex and often render current technologies inefficient, which results in a severe lack of data. Implementation of plasma codes becomes complicated due to variations in software and hardware architectures. A potential solution is to develop an abstraction layer to connect infrastructure to application codes. This BoF focuses on identifying the needs for development and standardization of an abstraction layer, and the relevant functionalities/data structures that would be most useful to abstract.

sessions.title: How Must HPC Education Change for a World Where AI Generates Our Code?
sessions.speakers: Julia Mullen, Tim Mattson, Albert Reuther, Weronika Filinger
sessions.description: In the near future (if not already) HPC software will be generated by AI. The question is not “if” we must adapt, but “how” we will adapt. Everything about our software will be impacted. In this BoF, we will focus on training: How does what we teach have to change to accommodate the necessary shift in skills in the AI era? We need ideas from across the community and people who will dedicate the time to debate these ideas, digest them, and produce a position paper to drive the change we need in HPC. It all starts with this BoF.

sessions.title: IO500: The High-Performance Storage Community
sessions.speakers: Andreas Dilger, Jean Luca Bez, Dean Hildebrand, Julian Kunkel, Jay Lofstead
sessions.description: The IO500 is the de facto benchmark standard for HPC storage. Official IO500 lists have been released at ISC and SC events since SC17 and now have over 300 entries. The purpose is to foster the high-performance storage community and ensure forward progress towards the common goals of creating, sharing, and benefiting from a large corpus of shared storage data. IO500 also serves as the largest repository of detailed HPC storage information for researchers and system designers to analyze and evaluate over time. A key BoF highlight is the presentation of the latest IO500 Production and Research lists.

sessions.title: Navigating Complexity: Achieving Performance Portability in the Evolving Landscape of Accelerated HPC Systems
sessions.speakers: Amit Ruhela, David Martin, Steffen Christgau, Hatem Ltaief, Clayton Hughes, Toshihiro Hanawa +6
sessions.description: With the increasing demand for AI in HPC, there has been a rapid rise in accelerated architectures, portable programming models, and frameworks. The already-daunting task of programming for interconnected accelerated systems has become even more complex. This BoF, organized by IXPUG, will focus on portable programming across a wide range of heterogeneous architectures—including Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, and ARM supporting diverse simulation, data analytics, and AI workloads. The session will explore key challenges, state-of-the-art solutions, and emerging best practices for programming across these systems, identifying common principles and methodologies that support development and long-term maintenance across sites, architectures, and scientific applications.

sessions.title: One Year After MPI 5.0: Impact and What's Next?
sessions.speakers: Martin Schulz
sessions.description: The Message Passing Interface (MPI) API is the most dominant programming approach for HPC environments. Its specification is driven by the MPI Forum, an open forum consisting of MPI developers, vendors, and users. This year, the MPI Forum published the latest version of the standard, MPI 5.0. We will take a look at the new features and will discuss what they mean for the users of MPI. We will also discuss ongoing work toward the next version of the MPI standard, with lightning talks from the working groups, and get feedback from the community.

sessions.title: Open OnDemand User Group Meeting
sessions.speakers: Alan Chalker, Julia Ma, Emily Moffat Sadeghi
sessions.description: This BoF is meant to be an open discussion to guide the future roadmap for Open OnDemand (openondemand.org), by getting feedback from the community on the prioritization of the various tasks planned for the next few years. OOD is extremely relevant to ongoing discussions within the HPC community about user interfaces and science gateways. The session leaders, all part of the OOD development team, will jointly develop the content for the presentation in advance to ensure a wide range of viewpoints and topics are presented. We will also consult with our user advisory group in advance for their suggestions.

sessions.title: OpenQSE: Building an Open Quantum-HPC Software Ecosystem
sessions.speakers: Thomas Naughton, Amir Shehata, Sebastian Stern, Yoonho Park, Michael Ferguson, Lukas Burgholzer +1
sessions.description: Quantum computing resources are increasingly integrated into HPC and cloud environments, but software stacks remain isolated, vendor-specific, and often proprietary. OpenQSE is a community effort developing an open, modular ecosystem of vendor-neutral specifications to close the interoperability gaps that fragment hybrid quantum-classical workflows. This BoF will briefly share the initiative's roadmap and working-group progress, then open the floor for structured discussion with HPC facility staff, application teams, vendors, and researchers to identify priorities and shape the direction together. The intended outcome is a prioritized set of integration artifacts the community identifies as most urgent for near-term development.

sessions.title: Operational Data Analytics: Agentic AI for HPC Facilities
sessions.track: Data Analytics, Profiling and Optimization Tools
sessions.speakers: Dong Dai, Kevin Menear, Avisek Naug, Keiji Yamamoto, Steven Farrell, Jeff Hanson +7
sessions.description: Operational data analytics (ODA) has become essential for understanding and optimizing HPC systems. However, converting the vast amounts of operational data they generate into actionable insights still requires significant manual effort and domain expertise. Agentic AI has the potential to extend traditional analytics by reading telemetry, correlating signals, diagnosing problems, and drafting fixes for an operator to approve. This BoF will explore the state of the art in agentic AI’s applicability to ODA, promising use cases, limitations, and governance challenges. Participants will share experiences and discuss how agentic AI can enhance future HPC operations and efficiency.

sessions.title: Photonics for AI and HPC: Breaking the Bandwidth and Power Barrier
sessions.speakers: Dan Olds, Phil Pokorny, Andy Mills, Preet Virk, Luis Ancajas
sessions.description: As AI and HPC systems scale to unprecedented levels, traditional electrical interconnects are becoming a limiting factor. Silicon photonics offers a promising path to address bandwidth, energy efficiency and interconnect scalability constraints, but questions remain around deployment readiness, integration complexity and ecosystem maturity. Led by industry analyst Dan Olds, this session brings together experts from Penguin Solutions, Marvell and Micron to explore photonic interconnects from multiple perspectives. Panelists will discuss the technology’s value today, the technical and operational challenges ahead, where photonics can make the greatest impact, and what the broader ecosystem must do to accelerate real-world adoption.

sessions.title: Talking to Your Users: Ask Better Questions Before You Build
sessions.speakers: Beth Cerny, Johanna Cohoon, Sarah Read, Jordan Frith, Charles Lively III,
sessions.description: User experience (UX) is often misunderstood as a nice-to-have, rather than a necessary element of scientific computing. In reality, UX encompasses all the ways a user interacts with a product and is highly relevant to HPC systems. This interactive BoF will introduce UX work as a practical approach for improving usability and adoption. Participants will discuss how to ask users better questions to uncover needs and identify opportunities to improve systems, services, and support. Participants will leave with practical methods, starter resources, and connections to a growing cross-institutional UX community. This session benefits developers, documentation specialists, and facility support staff.

sessions.title: Unified Communication X (UCX) Community
sessions.speakers: Gilad Shainer, Pavel Shamis, Oscar Hernandez
sessions.description: In order to exploit the capabilities of new HPC systems and to meet their demands in scalability, communication software needs to scale to millions of cores and support applications with adequate functionality. UCX is a collaboration between industry, national labs, and academia that consolidates and provides a unified open-source framework. The UCX project is managed by the UCF Consortium (http://www.ucfconsortium.org/). The session will serve as the UCX community meeting and will introduce the latest developments to HPC developers and the broader user community.

Our goal is to go beyond the individual contributions and…

sessions.title: AI and ML for HPC Workload Analysis: From Isolation to Reproducibility — Building Common Benchmarks
sessions.speakers: Kadidia Konate, Sergio Iserte, Kevin Menear, Estela Suarez, Ahmad Maroof Karimi
sessions.description: HPC facilities each build operational data analytics in isolation, with no shared benchmarks to compare methods or reproduce results across sites. This seventh-edition BoF convenes the community around a common goal: shared standards, open benchmarks, and cross-facility collaboration for HPC workload analysis. Using the HPC ODA Commons, introduced to the community at ISC 2026, as a working exemplar, we examine how standardized schemas and benchmark recipes enable reproducible comparison across systems. We present an emerging multi-facility study, invite sites to contribute data, schemas, or models, and work together to prioritize analyses and plan a community report.

sessions.title: Analog Computing for Science: From Emerging Technologies to a Shared Research Agenda
sessions.speakers: Antonino Tumeo, Johannes Gebert, Suma George Cardwell, Sara Achour, Josef Weidendorfer, Talya Vaknin +2
sessions.description: Analog computing is re-emerging as a broad approach to scientific computation, offering opportunities beyond energy efficiency, including low-latency physical dynamics, reduced data movement, computation integrated with sensing, and new methods for simulation, optimization, and artificial intelligence. Yet progress remains fragmented across physical substrates, applications, architectures, mathematics, and software. This highly interactive BoF will bring the SC community together to identify challenges, promising workloads, shared infrastructure, and opportunities for collaboration. Building on the DOE ASCR report Basic Research Needs for Analog Computing for Science, participants will prioritize research directions and help shape a community agenda for analog and hybrid analog-digital computing.

sessions.title: Hands-On Outreach: Bridging AI, Supercomputing, and the Public
sessions.speakers: Paige Kinsley, Spyro Nita, Darren White, Eleanor Broadway, Eva Fernandez Amez, Bryan Johnston +4
sessions.description: As AI rapidly reshapes public interest in computing, the HPC community has a unique opportunity to demystify these technologies and introduce foundational computational concepts. This interactive Birds of a Feather (BoF) session brings together HPC educators, trainers, and outreach practitioners to explore, facilitate, and evaluate hands-on AI outreach activities. Participants will test proven activities, discuss engagement best practices, and collaborate to design new resources using both human-led and AI-assisted frameworks. Attendees will walk away with a toolkit of reusable activities, insights into AI-driven content generation, and a collaborative network to strengthen HPC outreach community-wide.

sessions.title: Inference Services and Agents on HPC: Scaling Scientific AI for Academic Community
sessions.speakers: Dan Stanzione, Weicheng Huang, Venkatram Vishwanath, Jason Haga, Frank Würthwein, Thomas Hauser +4
sessions.description: Initiated at SC25 to explore AI inference services in the academic HPC community, this BoF returns to address the fast-evolving landscape of inference services, agentic AI, tool services, and AI4Science. This practitioner forum brings centers and researchers together to share practical insights and experiences spanning infrastructure, software, and use cases. This session aims to cultivate collaborative solutions for AI developments. The goal remains to foster a sustained, cross-institutional "community of practice" bridging academic and governmental HPC centers and the user community to foster collaborations in this area.

sessions.title: Key Features Coming to OpenMP API Version 6.1
sessions.speakers: Tim Mattson, Michael Klemm
sessions.description: The OpenMP Architecture Review Board releases new versions of OpenMP every 2-3 years. This year, we will release OpenMP API version 6.1 just before SC26. Feature champions from the OpenMP Language committee will highlight key features in the OpenMP API version 6.1 through short lightning talks with rounds of discussion to give participants ample opportunity to interact with OpenMP experts, ask questions, and provide feedback. We will also include talks from vendors supporting compilers to discuss timelines for support of OpenMP API features.

sessions.title: MLPerf: A Benchmark for Machine Learning
sessions.speakers: Tom St. John, Murali Emani, Miro Hodak, Tushar Krishna, Wolfgang De Salvador, David Kanter
sessions.description: As AI workloads scale exponentially, evaluating machine learning infrastructure requires rigorous, standardized benchmarking. This Birds of a Feather session brings together HPC researchers, hardware architects, and software engineers to discuss the future of the MLPerf benchmark suite. The discussion will address critical scaling challenges, heterogeneous accelerator evaluation, and performance metrics for disaggregated infrastructure. Participants will collaborate on driving reproducibility and expanding benchmarks to encompass emerging, complex AI workloads. Join us to share deployment insights and directly shape the benchmarking roadmaps guiding the next generation of supercomputing systems.

sessions.title: MPICH: A High-Performance Open-Source MPI Implementation
sessions.speakers: Hui Zhou, Ken Raffenetti, Nathaniel Shineman, Simon Pickartz, Naveen Namashivayam, Michael Wilkins +1
sessions.description: MPICH is one of the most widely used open-source implementations of the MPI standard and the foundation for many vendor MPI libraries powering today's HPC systems. This BoF brings together MPICH developers, industry partners, and HPC users to share the latest project developments, discuss support for emerging architectures and MPI features, and explore future directions for the MPI ecosystem. This year's session will also discuss opportunities for community engagement and contributions to MPICH. Attendees are encouraged to participate in an interactive format, ask questions, share experiences, and help shape the future of one of HPC's core software infrastructures.

sessions.title: Numerical Linear Algebra in the Age of Coding Agents
sessions.speakers: Maksim Melnichenko, Jack Dongarra, James Demmel, Piotr Luszczek, Hartwig Anzt, Michael Mahoney +7
sessions.description: Since SC25, a revolution has taken hold: coding agents have moved from curiosity into nearly every institution's pipeline, and "vibe coding" is now how much software, numerical included, gets written. That matters for numerical linear algebra (NLA), whose libraries underpin modern science and whose trustworthiness was built over 50 years of human expert engineering. Now, when a plausible NLA kernel is nearly free to generate, what holds that trust together? This BoF gathers established leaders and younger NLA scientists from academia and industry to open a discussion, so our community shapes this shift rather than being swept along.

sessions.title: Open Source and Sovereign Infrastructure for HPC and AI
sessions.speakers: Stig Telfer, Jonathan Mills, David Power, John Michael Lowe, Sadaf Alam, Wojciech Turek
sessions.description: Open source has long been at the heart of HPC infrastructure management. Traditional HPC platforms have been well served by software stacks designed to meet this specific purpose. A new era brings new demands for HPC and AI. Open source infrastructure management faces new challenges on many fronts. This session features leading practitioners of a new generation of software-defined open HPC-AI infrastructure. The session will present a diverse range of open source solutions for current use cases, including advantages and disadvantages. Common problems will be identified and solutions shared. Attendees will be invited to share their experiences.

sessions.title: Procurements Under Pressure: Adaptive Strategies for HPC Centers in an Uncertain World
sessions.speakers: Andrew Younge, Edgar Leon, Patrick Carribault, Scott Atchley, Dan Ernst, Satoshi Matsuoka +3
sessions.description: HPC computing centers face mounting procurement risks driven by geopolitical tensions, semiconductor supply constraints, and AI-driven demand for GPUs. Leading-edge fabrication is concentrated among a small number of fabs worldwide, leaving centers exposed when disruptions strike. What was once a predictable multi-year planning cycle has become a landscape of uncertainty. This BoF brings together center directors, vendors, and system integrators from across the international HPC community to develop shared adaptive strategies — from flexible RFPs to extended machine lifetimes. Community participation is central: the goal is not to deliver answers, but to build them together.

sessions.title: Quantum Jumps: From NISQ to FTQC to Hybrid HPC
sessions.speakers: Kevin Kissell, Dave Bacon, Katherine Klymko, Matthew Otten, Aaron Lott
sessions.description: Quantum computing is experiencing accelerating transitions, from noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices to fault-tolerant quantum computers, and from quantum computers being objects of research to their becoming scientific computation tools. Quantum programming habits and assumptions must be revisited, and for the HPC community, this is more than an incremental hardware upgrade; it affects entire stacks. This session will explore how compilation workflows, execution models, and algorithmic strategies are expected to change to incorporate error correction and integrate with production HPC workflows. Thought leaders from the quantum industry, HPC, and academic research will exchange perspectives and engage the audience in discussion.

sessions.title: Scientific Software and the People Who Make It Happen: Building Our Communities and Practices
sessions.speakers: David Bernholdt, Anshu Dubey, Robert Haines, Mozhgan Kabiri chimeh, Daniel Katz, Lauren Milechin +3
sessions.description: Software has become central to all aspects of modern science and technology. Especially in high performance computing (HPC) and computational science and engineering (CSE), it is becoming ever larger and more complex while computer platforms evolve and become more diverse. Simultaneously, the teams behind the software are becoming larger, more technically diverse, and more geographically distributed. AI tools add both great potential and significant caution. This BoF will address these issues and more, sharing experiences and best practices, and building community around software topics. Presentations and discussion notes will be made available at the BoF series website (http://bit.ly/swe-cse-bof).

sessions.title: The Green500: Trends in Energy-Efficient Supercomputing
sessions.speakers: Wu Feng, Erich Strohmaier, Natalie Bates, John Baron, Brandon Tran
sessions.description: With power being a first-order design constraint on par with performance, it is important to measure and analyze energy-efficiency trends in supercomputing. To raise the awareness of greenness as a first-order design constraint, the Green500 seeks to characterize the energy efficiency of supercomputers for different metrics, workloads, and methodologies. This BoF discusses trends across the Green500 and highlights from the current Green500 list. In addition, the Green500, Top500, and Energy Efficient HPC Working Group have been working together on improving power-measurement methodology, and this BoF presents updates that will improve ease of submission without compromising accuracy.

sessions.title: The International Post-Exascale (InPEx) Project
sessions.speakers: Bernd Mohr, Jérôme Bobin, Pete Beckman, Jack Dongarra, Satoshi Matsuoka, Mohamed Wahib +2
sessions.description: Several (trans-)national initiatives have recognized the crucial importance of co-design between hardware, software, and application stakeholders in the path to exascale and beyond. However, these regional efforts are somehow disconnected while the community would benefit by sharing return of experience, common know-how, and advancing on the new problems arising as exascale machines become more and more available. The International Post-Exascale (InPEx) Project will bring together researchers and engineers, companies, funding bodies, and policy organizations to contribute to the implementation of an international, shared, high-quality computing environment based on the principles and practices of co-design.

sessions.title: Ultra Ethernet: Next-Generation Networking for HPC Supercomputers and AI Factories
sessions.speakers: Torsten Hoefler, Eric Spada, Keith Underwood, Rip Sohan, Dhabaleswar K. (DK) Panda, Ron Brightwell
sessions.description: Ultra Ethernet has emerged as a major effort to create a scalable, open networking architecture for both AI factories and high-performance computing systems. As AI clusters continue to grow while HPC workloads demand ever-higher communication performance and efficiency, many networking requirements are beginning to converge. This BoF provides a forum for researchers, system architects, operators, application developers, and network vendors to discuss experiences, emerging requirements, unresolved challenges, and future directions for large-scale networking. The discussion aims to identify common needs across HPC and AI and foster collaboration toward open, interoperable networking solutions for next-generation computing systems.

sessions.title: Who Shapes the Future of Public HPC? Planning, Priorities, and Investment in the Age of AI and Quantum Computing
sessions.speakers: Florian Berberich, Kengo NAKAJIMA, Yutong Lu, Happy Sithole, John Towns, Katerina Antypas +1
sessions.description: HPC infrastructures are being reshaped by rapid hardware innovation, pressure for greater energy efficiency, and the rise of AI and data-intensive workloads. Simultaneously, future directions are influenced not only by scientific communities and public research agendas, but also by industry roadmaps and emerging QC ambitions. This BoF will examine how different countries plan future public HPC investments, how priorities are set, and who has influence in that process. The aim is to better understand whether public HPC remains community-driven or is increasingly shaped by industrial and market forces, and what this means for the future of research infrastructures.

This BoF session brings together HPC systems engineers, data center architects, and site reliability engineers to discuss the architecture, integration challenges, and best practices for building robust telemetry pipelines around OpenCHAMI, ensuring operational visibility, rapid fault isolation, and open-source compliance in next-generation supercomputing environments.

sessions.title: HPC Next: Reflections and Progress on the RISC-V Ecosystem
sessions.speakers: Nick Brown, Daniele Gregori, Doug Norton, Yiftach Gilad, Tom Gall, Andreas Herten +1
sessions.description: RISC-V is an open standard instruction set architecture (ISA) enabling the open development of CPUs and a shared software ecosystem. There are already over 30 billion RISC-V cores, which are accelerating rapidly. Nonetheless, for all the successes that RISC-V has enjoyed, it is yet to become popular in HPC. Recent advances, however, such as data center RISC-V-based CPUs and PCIe accelerators, mean that this technology is becoming a more realistic proposition for our workloads. This BoF aims to connect the RISC-V and HPC communities. We will explore how the technology is progressing and identify lessons learnt from previous years' predictions.

sessions.title: HPC User Support in the AI and Exascale Era
sessions.speakers: Haritha Siddabathuni Som, Rebecca Hartman-Baker, Chris Fuson, Smita Darmora, Thomas Breuer, Helena Vela Beltran +1
sessions.description: As HPC enters an era of extreme heterogeneity and AI integration, user support is a critical strategic enabler. However, rising system complexity and finite staffing strain traditional models. To thrive in the AI and exascale era, a collaborative community approach is essential. This BoF session invites practitioners, providers, and users to collaboratively reshape HPC support. Featuring insights from facility leaders on managing rapid AI adoption, an interactive live survey, and open group discussions, participants will share experiences regarding scaling, AI automation, and knowledge transfer. Outcomes will form a post-conference report dedicated to fostering a sustainable, community-driven support ecosystem.

sessions.title: Open MPI State of the Union 2026
sessions.speakers: George Bosilca, Howard Pritchard, Edgar Gabriel
sessions.description: Open MPI continues to advance portable, high-performance communication for increasingly heterogeneous, accelerator-rich systems and workloads. Over the past year, the community has advanced MPI-5.0 conformance, expanded accelerator support, improved collective performance, and worked with partners across the HPC ecosystem. We'll discuss what Open MPI has accomplished over the past year and present a roadmap for the next year. One of Open MPI's strengths lies in its diversity: we represent many different viewpoints across the HPC community. To that end, many developers from the community will be present to discuss and answer your questions both during and after the BoF.

sessions.title: Real-Time Scientific Data Streaming to HPC Nodes: Challenges and Innovations VI
sessions.speakers: Bjoern Enders, Adam Thompson, Alex Upton, Rafael Ferreira da Silva, Eli Dart, Rajive Joshi +1
sessions.description: Emerging scientific needs are driving a new class of workflows that require near real-time processing, urgent computing, and time-sensitive decision-making. The traditional "compute-store-analyze" paradigm, which relies on dumping massive datasets to file systems for post-processing, has become an unsustainable bottleneck. It introduces unacceptable latency, and often renders high-frequency data analysis practically impossible. This BoF discusses this challenge by exploring the architectural shift from file-based workflows to high-performance streaming. In this new paradigm, storage is treated not as a buffer for post-processing, but as a sink for final scientific results, while analysis, visualization, and reduction occur in-transit or in-situ.

sessions.title: The Future of Dynamic Resource Utilization in HPC: Chances and Challenges
sessions.speakers: Martin Schreiber, Martin Schulz, Antonio Peña, Daniel Milroy, Dominik Huber, Jesus Carretero +3
sessions.description: The increasing computational demands are driving the deployment of ever-larger HPC and AI infrastructures. While these systems deliver unprecedented performance, they also pose critical challenges to their efficient use, particularly in terms of energy consumption. This BoF will explore dynamic resource management as a key enabler of higher utilization and reduced energy consumption. Instead of traditional batch scheduling, dynamic resource control at the start or during a job’s runtime enables better allocation of compute capacity, memory, network availability, and storage. This BoF will address the two major key challenges of novel scheduling and its integration across the software stack.

sessions.title: The Future of NSF-Supported Advanced Cyberinfrastructure
sessions.speakers: Katie Antypas, Wen-Wen Tung, Marlon Pierce, Andrey Kanaev, Alejandro Suarez
sessions.description: The U.S. National Science Foundation's vision and investment plans for cyberinfrastructure (CI) are designed to address the evolving needs of the science and engineering research community. Senior leadership and program staff from NSF’s Office of Advanced Cyberinfrastructure (OAC) will discuss OAC's vision, strategic and national priorities, as well as highlights from the latest funding opportunities across all aspects of the research cyberinfrastructure ecosystem. Substantial time will be devoted to audience Q&A between attendees and NSF staff and unstructured time to meet informally with NSF staff.

sessions.title: The State of Open-Source Computer Architecture Simulators: Shared Problems and Community Action
sessions.speakers: Jack Jones, Jens Domke, Kevin Brown, Caitlin Ross, Kentaro Sano, Priyanka Sharma +2
sessions.description: Computer architecture simulators are central to exploring the design space of modern high-performance hardware and analyzing its performance. Many open-source simulators exist, targeting different hardware scopes, granularities, and metrics, yet none is perfect: issues with speed, accuracy, and usability limit their effectiveness for architecture researchers, accelerator designers, hardware-software co-designers, and performance engineers, among others. This BoF convenes an expert panel of users and developers from academia and industry to discuss these tools' shortcomings and possible responses. We invite all who build, use, or depend on these simulators to join the discussion and identify impactful community efforts, with outcomes shared publicly.

sessions.title: Three Axes for Scientific AI on HPC: Energy Efficiency, Uncertainty, and Verifiable Trust
sessions.speakers: Olivera Kotevska, Antigoni Georgiadou, Tushar Athawale, Arthur Lorenzon, Peter Coveney, Haotong Qin +1
sessions.description: Scientific AI on leadership-class HPC sits at the intersection of three concerns the community usually addresses separately: energy efficiency, uncertainty quantification (UQ), and verifiable trust. Compression and quantization change model behavior in ways that matter for scientific validity. Energy optimizations can quietly erode privacy and safety properties. And the HPC, UQ, and AI-safety communities rarely meet in one room. This BoF session brings them together to identify shared challenges, gaps in current practice, and concrete next steps toward AI systems for science that are simultaneously efficient, uncertainty-aware, and verifiably trustworthy on the world’s largest computing systems.

sessions.title: Trusted Research Environments for AI and Integrated Science: Launching the Genesis Mission
sessions.speakers: Ben Brown, Jeremy Crampton, Lois Curfman McInnes, Deborah Bard, Arjun Shankar, Sadaf Alam +1
sessions.description: This BoF aims to build on the successful launch at SC25 of a multi-national community of practice. This year we focus on the Genesis Mission and DOE’s American Science Cloud and AI Models Consortium projects, to include establishing best practices for multi-facility or multi-institutional workflows, lessons learned from international contexts, sharing and accessing resources, developing mixed public/private partnerships, and protecting sensitive data privacy and security. Our goal is to advance progress in developing secure and trustworthy infrastructures for AI and integrated science. We seek to understand trustworthiness in supercomputing environments from both technical and socio-technical perspectives.

sessions.title: Trustworthy Data at Scale: HDF5 in the Age of AI-Driven Science
sessions.speakers: Michael Breitenfeld, Elena Pourmal, Suren Byna, Quincey Koziol, Anthony Kougkas
sessions.description: HDF5 has anchored HPC I/O for 25 years, and AI-driven science is redefining what "trustworthy data at scale" demands: verifiable provenance, concurrent I/O, and cloud-native interoperability. Short talks from domain scientists launch interactive segments where an opt-in agentic survey captures attendee priorities, pain points, and open questions in real time, with aggregate results used to steer the discussion. This session is for seasoned HDF5 developers and domain scientists, and anyone just starting out or wondering what HDF5 is about: bring the problems you'd like to solve, and help steer the discussion and provide input to future HDF5 roadmap planning.

sessions.title: Watts, FLOPs, and Impact: Rethinking Energy in the Exascale Era
sessions.track: Power and Energy, State of the Practice, Sustainability
sessions.speakers: Sameh Abdulah, Bilel Hadri, Natalie Bates, Steven Martin, Siddhartha Jana, Mathis Bode +1
sessions.description: Energy consumption has become a key constraint in high performance computing (HPC), shaping system design, procurement, software, and scientific workflows in the exascale era. As large-scale simulations and AI-driven workloads increase power demand, the community must reconsider how performance is measured, optimized, and reported beyond FLOPs alone. This BoF session will convene researchers, facility operators, vendors, and application scientists to discuss energy measurement, performance-per-watt metrics, efficient algorithms and runtimes, workload scheduling, and carbon-aware computing. The session will identify practical gaps, share lessons from production systems, and define community priorities for sustainable, energy-efficient HPC at scale.
